name: WHO guidance on heat illness at events
headline: WHO releases guidance on preventing heat-related illness at mass gatherings
summary: On 30 September 2026 the WHO released a resource suite on preventing and managing heat-related illness at mass gatherings.
keyPoints: The WHO released the guidance suite on 30 September 2026.
The WHO's evidence review of studies from 1980 to 2025 found nearly half a million medical encounters at mass gatherings, including more than 22,000 heat-related illnesses.
The suite includes a heat-risk assessment tool, and WHO names spectators, attendees, volunteers and workers among those affected by heat at mass gatherings.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 30 September 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) released a resource suite called "Prevention and management of heat-related illness at mass gatherings". The WHO says most heat-related illnesses at major events can be prevented or treated on site when timely risk management measures are in place.

Its evidence review of studies from 1980 to 2025 found nearly half a million medical encounters at mass gatherings, including more than 22,000 heat-related illnesses.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The guidance includes a heat-risk assessment tool and is intended to complement the WHO's heat-health action plan guidance and existing national plans. The WHO urges governments, event organisers and partners to build heat risk management into health planning and event operations.

source.title: WHO releases new guidance to prevent heat-related illness at mass gatherings
